userStories.title: Dispatch input accepts FIX
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add FIX to the fleet API/protocol contract and normalize its PR-derived dispatch input.

**Motivation** — Today koda reviews a PR (K1), feeds decisions in and remembers withdrawn findings (K2), but the findings the review agreed with are fixed by hand or by `nax bot fix` run from a person's machine under their own login, outside koda's audit, budget and runner fleet.

**Approach** — **Same feature as `REVIEW`.** A `FIX`'s feature is `review-pr-<n>` (`reviewFeature`), so the existing active-feature index makes a `FIX` while a `REVIEW` or `FIX` of that PR is active a 409, and the reverse. `prNumberOfReviewFeature` keeps working for both.

`packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts` (types only): `FleetJobKindName` (line 123) adds `'FIX'`; `RunnerCapabilities` (lines 64-92) adds `botFix?: true`; `SnapshotEventPayload` (line ~143) adds `fixOutcome?: 'pushed' | 'nothing'`. `AssignPayload.review` is unchanged and is now sent for `FIX` too. This story lands these shared types; sending FIX assignments is US-003.

Target: `FIX` takes the same branch with the same checks; each reason names the dispatched command (`prNumber required for FIX`, `feature is derived for FIX`, `planFrom is only for PLAN`, `ref is the default branch for FIX`, `bashMode must be raw for FIX`, `ticketRefs is not for FIX`); for `RUN`/`PLAN` the two reasons become `feature is reserved for REVIEW and FIX` and `prNumber is only for REVIEW and FIX`.

Run bun run generate from the repository root to update openapi.json and the CLI client; never hand-edit generated files.

**Scope** — In: API enums, dispatch DTO/normalization, types-only shared protocol additions and generated contract artifacts. Dispatching `REVIEW` or `FIX` from the CLI, from the assistant tool `koda_dispatch_job`, or from the web dispatch form, and a `Fix` action on a `REVIEW` job page; part B. A `FIX` needs both: `capabilityMisfit` returns `bot_review` without `botReview`, then `bot_fix` without `botFix`. `bot_fix` is not permanent. userStories.title: Review memory from FIX jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Feed the review inside a runner-verdict FIX into existing K2 review-memory ingestion.

**Motivation** — Today koda reviews a PR (K1), feeds decisions in and remembers withdrawn findings (K2), but the findings the review agreed with are fixed by hand or by `nax bot fix` run from a person's machine under their own login, outside koda's audit, budget and runner fleet.

**Approach** — **Review memory.** Bundle ingest reads the review artifact of a `REVIEW` in `COMPLETED` (unchanged) or of a `FIX` in `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED` (the review posted even when the fix failed), with the current lease epoch. A `FIX` in `ESCALATED` or `CRASHED` is not read (no runner verdict was reached). `parseBotReview` already refuses a bundle whose `nax.stdout` lacks the artifact line when several artifacts exist; with one artifact and no line it reads that one, unchanged.

`BundleIngestService.write` (`apps/api/src/fleet/ingest/bundle-ingest.service.ts:103-104`) — Baseline: `job.command === 'REVIEW' && job.state === 'COMPLETED' && job.leaseEpoch === claim.leaseEpoch`. Target: that, or `job.command === 'FIX'` in `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` or `CANCELLED` with `job.leaseEpoch === claim.leaseEpoch`.

Keep artifact selection, trusted-event validation, existing recordForJob deduplication and post-commit minter notification unchanged; only broaden the command/state eligibility predicate. write is private; exercise its parseBundle options through ingestOne(now) with an injected claim/store/job and a parseBundle spy, following the existing review event ingest harness rather than exporting write. Extend bundle-ingest.service.spec.ts review event ingest cases and the existing fleet-review-events-ingest.integration.spec.ts real bundle/queue fixtures. Use the shared DB gate and verify actual PG runs outside the sandbox.

**Scope** — In: FIX current-epoch eligibility and its connection to existing review event ingestion. Out: decision selection at dispatch (US-002), runner review spawning (US-008), FIX verdict (US-012), new memory abstractions, RUN-only knowledge outcomes and analytics read models.

**Goal** — Apply bot cost caps to REVIEW/FIX and construct full-review/fix argv with one exact remainder helper.

This is a behaviour change for `REVIEW`: a manual or auto-review's `maxCostUsd` (K1-B `autoReviewMaxCostUsd`) now bounds the review, where nax used its own default before. userStories.title: Fix step chaining
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Chain the fix after this JobRun's successful review while preserving process ownership, cancellation and halt semantics.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix` refuses unless a `bot-review.json` of the PR's exact current head is under its own output dir (`loadLatestReview(outputDir, pr, headSha)`, nax `src/bot/fix-input.ts:69`). Every koda job has its own output dir, so a `FIX` must run its own review first.

**Approach** — **One job, two nax processes, chained by the runner.** The runner spawns step 1 (the review) as today's `REVIEW` spawn does. When step 1's process has exited, the job is not cancelled and `nax.stdout` has the review `artifact` line, the runner spawns step 2 (the fix) in the same RUNNING phase, writes its output to `<jobDir>/fix.stdout` and `<jobDir>/fix.stderr`, records the new `pid`/`pgid` on the journal row and watches it to exit. Only then does the job go UPLOADING and terminal. No journal column is added: `fix.stdout` existing marks step 2 as started.

**Chaining only in the session that started step 1.** `JobRun` chains step 2 only when this `JobRun` spawned step 1 (`lifecycle` entered through `prepare` or `reprepare`). A readopted `FIX` (`watch` or `finish`) never starts step 2: when its step-1 process exits, or is already gone, it is judged (call 4), which gives `interrupted before fix` when the review posted. The token cache does not survive a restart, so a resumed step 2 could not be trusted to authenticate. A `FIX` joins the `PLAN`/`REVIEW` readopt branch (watch a live process that is ours, else finish). **Recording and signalling step 2.** The new `pid`/`pgid` are patched on the journal row as soon as `spawnFixStep` resolves, before any halt or cancel check, so `killIfOurs` and `sendTerm` always see the live process. If a cancel was requested while `spawnFixStep` ran, the runner sends SIGTERM to the new `pgid` even when step 1 was already signalled: both one-shot guards (`cancelSentAtMs` and `sigkilled`) reset for the new process group, so a step 2 that ignores SIGTERM is still escalated to SIGKILL. If the run halts (ABANDON, daemon stop) while `spawnFixStep` ran, the patch still happens and the loop then returns as any halted watch does.

Runner `JobRun.watchUntilExit` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/job-run.ts:384`) — Target: for a `FIX` whose step 1 this `JobRun` spawned (call 2), when the watched process has exited, `hasFixStep` is false, no cancel is requested, `readReviewPosted` is true and `fixBudgetRemainder` is not `null`, it calls `executor.spawnFixStep(row)` once, patches `pid`/`pgid` per call 2 and keeps watching the new process; a throw is held as the step-2 failure for the verdict and the loop ends without a retry.

A `readReviewPosted` throw gives `review not posted` (and never chains). Treat it as false for the FIX chaining guard only; do not change REVIEW's read-error behavior. Use the shared string-based fixBudgetRemainder and suppress chaining on undefined ledger. The prior-SIGKILL regression AC exercises reset of both one-shot guards at a simulated process handoff with prior signal history; it must not be implemented by relaxing the rule that a cancel observed before chaining prevents spawning. Pass held spawn failure to US-012's judge instead of failSafe. Extend job-run.spec.ts with real SQLite, fake time and delayed spawn promises; keep FakeExecutor changes compatible with US-009/011.

**Scope** — In: lifecycle eligibility flag, single chain attempt, new process journaling, guard reset, cancellation/halt races and held step-2 failure. Out: spawning implementation (US-009), file outcome parsing (US-011), terminal verdict mapping (US-012), live fix logs. Resuming step 2 after a runner restart; such a job ends `interrupted before fix`. A second fix round in one job, and the nax post-push re-review (the job always passes `--no-rereview`). The no-resume boundary forbids starting another fix process after restart; readopt may still watch a process whose handle was already recorded, without chaining a new one.

**Interface** — `executor.spawnFixStep(row)`; `executor.hasFixStep(job): Promise<boolean>`; `fixBudgetRemainder(maxCostUsd: string, spentUsd: string | undefined): number | null`.

userStories.title: FIX verdict
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Judge FIX from ordered file evidence and report final cost, outcome and optional full pushed SHA.

**Motivation** — Today koda reviews a PR (K1), feeds decisions in and remembers withdrawn findings (K2), but the findings the review agreed with are fixed by hand or by `nax bot fix` run from a person's machine under their own login, outside koda's audit, budget and runner fleet.

**Approach** — **Verdict** (checked in order, from files; nax runs detached so there is no exit code):

| condition | job state | reason / recorded |
|:--|:--|:--|
| cancel requested | `CANCELLED` | |
| `nax.stdout` has no `nax bot review: artifact ` line | `FAILED` | `review not posted` |
| step 2 failed to start | `FAILED` | `fix spawn failed: <message>` |
| no `fix.stdout`, `fixBudgetRemainder` is `null` and the spend was known | `FAILED` | `budget spent by review` |
| no `fix.stdout`, `fixBudgetRemainder` is `null` and the spend was `undefined` | `FAILED` | `cost ledger unreadable` |
| no `fix.stdout` otherwise | `FAILED` | `interrupted before fix` |
| `fix.stdout` has a line starting `nax bot fix: PR #<n> — pushed ` | `COMPLETED` | `fixOutcome` `pushed`, `resultSha` |
| `fix.stdout` has a line starting `nax bot fix: PR #<n> — nothing to fix` | `COMPLETED` | `fixOutcome` `nothing`, `resultSha` when present |
| otherwise | `FAILED` | first non-empty line of `fix.stderr`, trimmed to 200 characters; `fix not pushed` when there is none |

`<n>` is the job's PR number. `resultSha` is the `pushedSha` of the fix run's `bot-state.json` (the directory of the path on the `nax bot fix: log ` line), only when it matches `^[0-9a-f]{40}$`; the 7-character stdout sha is never reported. A `nothing` outcome with an advisor-ledger push therefore reports that push's sha. The `log` path is used only when it resolves inside `<jobDir>/nax-out/bot/pr-<n>/`; any other path gives no `resultSha`. A requested cancel is checked before any file is read, so it always ends `CANCELLED`, as for `REVIEW`. Unlike `REVIEW` (whose judge lets a read error reach `failSafe`), a `FIX` read that throws is treated as that file saying nothing: a `readReviewPosted` throw gives `review not posted` (and never chains), and a `readFixOutcome` throw gives `fix not pushed`.

Runner `JobRun.judge` (`job-run.ts:410`): a `FIX` branch beside `REVIEW` returns call 4's verdict and a snapshot with `costSpentUsd`, and, on `COMPLETED`, `fixOutcome` and `resultSha` when present.

**No `resultPrUrl` or `resultBranch` for `FIX`, and no commit link.** The design doc put the PR URL in `resultPrUrl` and asked for a commit link; this spec does neither. The job page already shows `resultSha` (its first 12 characters, `jobs/[id]/index.vue:341`), which is enough for K3. `jobOutcomeOf` turns `COMPLETED` + `resultPrUrl` into a `pr_opened` notification, and PR attribution treats `resultPrUrl` as a PR the job opened. A `FIX` opens no PR. The web derives the PR from the job's feature, as for `REVIEW`.

Use only executor.hasFixStep/readReviewPosted/readFixOutcome/readPlanCost, never direct fix file reads in JobRun. The cost ledger is cumulative across both steps; use the shared string-based fixBudgetRemainder when no step marker exists. A held spawn failure from US-010 has precedence over missing-file budget/interruption cases and is not replaced by failSafe. Cancellation wins before result readers, including if they would throw. finish already preserves judged.snapshot with conditional truthy result-field overlays; reuse this merge for FIX's resultSha rather than adding a special push path or changing null handling. The verdict ACs exercise private judge through JobRun.start and emitted journal state/snapshot events; do not expose judge or read files directly in JobRun for tests. Unless an AC specifies an earlier failure, FIX outcome fixtures have no cancellation, a posted review, no held spawn failure and hasFixStep true. Extend job-run.spec.ts, leaving REVIEW behavior unchanged.

**Scope** — In: ordered FIX judge branch, held-error consumption, cumulative cost and successful outcome/SHA snapshot through finish. Out: producing/parsing files (US-008/009/011), API mirroring (US-004), new process chaining (US-010), The follow-up `REVIEW` koda queues after a `pushed` fix; part B (`fleet-pr-fix-surfaces`). Part B must also settle the K1-B head poller dispatching its own review of the pushed head. `resultPrUrl`, `resultBranch` and a commit link for `FIX` jobs; the PR is derived from the feature and the job page's existing sha display is kept.

**Interface** — `readFixOutcome(job): Promise<FixOutcome>`; `FixOutcome = { kind: 'pushed' | 'nothing' | 'none'; logPath: string | null; pushedSha: string | null; stderrLine: string | null }`; `fixBudgetRemainder(maxCostUsd: string, spentUsd: string | undefined): number | null`; completion snapshot `fixOutcome?: 'pushed' | 'nothing'` plus `resultSha` when present.
